site_name: AWS Susquehanna data center campus (former Cumulus Data campus), Salem Township
serving_utility: None in 2025 (behind the meter at Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant); PPL Electric Utilities delivers once the front-of-the-meter transition happens (begins spring 2026, full transition expected spring 2027)
load_basis: Contract ramp schedule, not a metered figure: Talen's CEO said on the Q1 2025 call (May 2025) that the campus was electrified and that the schedule over 2025 was to ramp up to 120 MW; AWS commitments ramp in 120 MW increments starting in 2025. No Talen filing fetched states MW actually delivered in 2025.
notes: Same campus as known fid osm:way/1334234458 (Amazon AWS PHL); coordinates are ours/OSM, not independently re-derived. Talen sold the Cumulus campus to AWS on 2024-03-04; Cumulus phase 1 shell was completed Jan 2023 but Talen first described AWS load as electrified in May 2025, so 2025 is used as first commercial operation (medium). Through 2025 the campus was served directly from Susquehanna under the 300 MW co-located ISA (FERC rejected raising it to 480 MW in Nov 2024). June 2025 amended PPA: up to 1,920 MW from Susquehanna through 2042 (840-1,200 MW by 2029, 1,680-1,920 MW by 2032), with Talen as retail supplier and PPL Electric handling transmission and delivery (https://www.powermag.com/talen-amazon-launch-18b-nuclear-ppa-a-grid-connected-ipp-model-for-the-data-center-era/). Talen's FY2025 10-K says the previously behind-the-meter load was moved into PJM's load forecast. The 960 MW buildout is the campus figure from the 2024 sale (https://www.power-eng.com/nuclear/aws-acquires-data-center-campus-connected-to-susquehanna-nuclear-station/); the 1,920 MW PPA may also cover other AWS sites in Pennsylvania.

operator: Talen Energy (Nautilus Cryptomine LLC; TeraWulf held 25% until Oct 2024)
serving_utility: None (behind the meter at Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant)
load_basis: Closed during 2025: Talen's Q2 2025 10-Q (Note 7, Nautilus Derecognition) says that in June 2025 the company ceased use of the Nautilus facility under the revised AWS PPA transition terms and that AWS will demolish it. Zero is the end-of-2025 load, not the 2025 average.
notes: Also covers known fid osm:way/1334234455 (second Nautilus building). Operated roughly March 2023 to June 2025, so it WAS load in 2023 and 2024 (EPRI's 2024 estimate may include it) and for about half of 2025. Capacity while operating is not pinned to a primary source fetched here: Cointelegraph (2023-03-07) describes phase one as a 180 MW facility with TeraWulf's share 50 MW; press coverage of the Oct 2024 buyout calls it a 200 MW facility (Data Center Dynamics page returned 403 and was not read). Treat ~180-200 MW as capacity, not metered load. County from the adjacent AWS campus sourcing (Luzerne); coordinates are ours/OSM.

site_name: Midland data center (Mawson Infrastructure, renamed Big Digital Energy)
operator: Big Digital Energy (formerly Mawson Infrastructure Group)
load_basis: Built power capacity, not metered load: June 2024 release says the expanded Midland site is about 120 MW (about 38,810 miner slots); the FY2025 10-K gives about 129 MW total current capacity across the company's sites (Midland plus the 8.8 MW Bellefonte site). The same 10-K reports the loss of a major colocation customer, so actual 2025 draw may be well below capacity.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities. Bitcoin self-mining and hosting/colocation. Address: the FY2025 10-K gives 950 Railroad Avenue, Midland, PA 15059 as principal place of business and says the company leases 8 acres in Midland where the data center sits; coordinates are the Census geocoder match for that address and assume the facility is at that address. Delivering utility NOT verified: the 10-K names Energy Harbor LLC as the energy supplier to the Midland facility (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1218683/000121390026037417/ea0281617-10k_mawson.htm) but no fetched source names the wires utility; Midland is in Beaver County, where Duquesne Light is the likely distribution utility (unverified, territory inference only). Start year: Energytech (2023-02-17) says the site was operating at 50 MW in December 2022 and adding a second 50 MW; site was announced Sept 2021, so first energization could be late 2021 or 2022. Mawson's Bellefonte, PA site (8.8 MW self-mining, lease from May 2023) is below the 10 MW cutoff and not listed separately.

site_name: Scrubgrass campus (bitcoin mining at the Scrubgrass waste-coal plant)
operator: Keel Infrastructure (formerly Bitfarms; Stronghold Digital Mining until March 2025)
load_basis: Energized capacity per Keel/Bitfarms FY2025 10-K site table (dated 2026-03-27): Scrubgrass 63 MW, flagged as not under an ESA with a utility and currently used for Bitcoin mining. Capacity, not metered average load.
notes: The known OSM fids osm:way/1539600946 through 1539600972 and osm:way/1539603377 through 1539603382 (about 36 small buildings at 41.271,-79.813) are all mining containers on this one campus; treat them as a single site. Location: Stronghold 10-K places the Scrubgrass Plant on a 650-acre site in Scrubgrass Township, Venango County (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1856028/000162828024010049/sdig-20231231.htm); coordinates are the centroid of the OSM container cluster. Mining load is co-located with the ~83.5 MW waste-coal plant (a PURPA qualifying facility that also sells into PJM); Stronghold said it could also buy grid power through a retail supplier, so some load may be grid-imported. Wires utility not named in any fetched filing; a Stronghold release refers to the Penelec zone of PJM, so Penelec (FirstEnergy) is the likely interconnecting utility (unverified). Start year: The Block (2021-08-03) reports 1,840 miners already operating at Scrubgrass; mining may have begun earlier than 2021. 1,363 MW is Keel's 'identified additional' pipeline for the site (750 MW of load studies submitted), not contracted.

site_name: Panther Creek campus (bitcoin mining at the Panther Creek waste-coal plant)
operator: Keel Infrastructure (formerly Bitfarms; Stronghold Digital Mining until March 2025)
serving_utility: PPL Electric Utilities (interconnection; 2025 mining load is co-located with the on-site plant, not firm retail service)
load_basis: Energized capacity per Keel/Bitfarms FY2025 10-K site table (dated 2026-03-27): Panther Creek 60 MW, flagged as not under an ESA and currently used for Bitcoin mining; Q3 2025 results describe an existing 60 MW ISA with PPL. Capacity, not metered average load.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities. Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap feature 'Panther Creek Energy Facility, Nesquehoning, Carbon County' (way 857195848, via Nominatim). Mining load sits with the ~80 MW waste-coal plant (PURPA qualifying facility). Keel reports 350 MW of contracted firm power under an ESA with PPL for a planned HPC/AI campus and expansion to about 510 MW; none of that was energized in 2025. Start year: Stronghold acquired the plant in Nov 2021 and its FY2021 10-K reports about 10,500 miners deployed at Panther Creek as of 2022-03-24, so first hashing was late 2021 or early 2022.

load_basis: Energized capacity per Keel/Bitfarms FY2025 10-K: 12 MW energized January 2025, plus 18 MW in May 2025, for 30 MW; used for Bitcoin mining in 2025 and being converted to HPC/AI. Capacity, not metered average load.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE: the centroid of Clark Street in Sharon (press reports place the 18-acre former Westinghouse site along Clark Street; no street number was found). Utility not named in any fetched source; the 10-K says a further 80 MW is under an ESA and expected by end of 2026 or first half of 2027 (the filing gives both). Sharon is in FirstEnergy's Penn Power area, so Penn Power is the likely utility (unverified, territory inference only). Keel bought the property from its landlord in late 2025.

site_name: Iron Mountain WPA-1 (Western Pennsylvania underground data center), Boyers
serving_utility: FirstEnergy (operating company not stated on the operator page; West Penn Power or Penn Power)
load_basis: Operator page: '15.5 MW total capacity with N+1 redundancy' for the 330,000 sq ft facility. This is total built/designed capacity; the page does not say how much is in use.
notes: Address 1137 Branchton Rd, Boyers, PA 16020 (operator page); the Census geocoder and Nominatim returned no match, so lat/lon are left null (our known point for bi:1221-0 is about 2 km away and is assumed to be the same campus; operator match only). The operator page claims over 30 years of colocation at the site, so our 2025 start year for this fid reflects a permit date, not first operation; actual first year not found. 'Retail' is assumed from the operator's description of FirstEnergy utility service with redundant feeds.

load_basis: Operator page lists 5 MW critical IT load (47,100 IT sq ft) for PIT2 at 35 Summit Park Dr, Pittsburgh, PA 15275. Built critical IT capacity, not metered load.
notes: Below the 10 MW cutoff; included only because it corrects a known facility we currently count at 14.2 MW. Match to bi:865-0 rests on operator name and the Summit Park address being consistent with our point (40.4516,-80.1901); the Census geocoder returned no match for the address, so lat/lon are null. DataBank's other Pittsburgh site, PIT1 (100 S Commons), lists 1.9 MW. Utility not stated by the operator (Duquesne Light territory is likely; unverified).

site_name: H5 Data Centers Philadelphia (1500 Spring Garden St)
notes: No load figure published. Operator page (https://h5datacenters.com/philadelphia-data-center.html) lists 72,000 sq ft and '7.5 MW generator backup power' for H5's space at 1500 Spring Garden St, Suite 520; that is backup nameplate, not load, and it suggests our 18 MW for this fid is high unless the permit covers other tenants in the same building. Utility not stated (PECO territory is likely; unverified). Year opened not stated.

No load figure published. Operator page (https://www.tierpoint.com/data-centers/pennsylvania/allentown-tekpark/) lists 122,000+ total sq ft, 96,000+ sq ft raised floor, and 'fifteen 2.5 MW and eight 2 MW redundant generators' (53.5 MW backup nameplate, with redundancy), on a 137-acre campus with dual 69 kV utility transmission feeds. Backup nameplate is not load. Utility not named by the operator (PPL Electric territory is likely; unverified). Year opened not stated. Probably the largest conventional colocation site in the state by generator fleet.

No load figure published. Operator page (https://www.tierpoint.com/data-centers/pennsylvania/valley-forge/) lists 137,000+ total sq ft, 61,000+ sq ft raised floor and 'nine 2.5 MW redundant generators' (22.5 MW backup nameplate including redundancy). Our current 27 MW for this fid exceeds the site's entire stated generator nameplate, so it is very likely too high. Utility not named (PECO territory is likely; unverified). Year opened not stated.

site_name: Iron City No. 1 Power Generator and Compute Center
notes: Not established as operating in 2025; do not assign 2025 load. PA DEP issued an air-quality plan approval to Iron City Wells, LLC for 15 natural gas-fired generators to power a computing center (described as an A.I. data center) in Karthaus Township, Clearfield County; notice in the 2026-01-31 Pennsylvania Bulletin, application received June 2025 per press coverage. Generator sizes and total MW not stated in the sources fetched. On-site gas generation implies behind-the-meter supply, but that is an inference (low). OSM tags give the address as 3160 Paul Hoddman Road, Karthaus.
